[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Mastering Caching Strategies in GitHub Actions"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Efficient dependency management is critical for fast and reliable CI/CD pipelines. As your project grows, downloading and installing dependencies on every workflow run can add significant delays. GitHub Actions provides the actions/cache mechanism to persist dependencies and speed up builds."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding actions/cache"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The actions/cache action allows you to cache dependencies such as node_modules, pip packages, or Gradle builds. It saves a designated directory and restores it in future workflow runs based on a unique cache key."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Key components include 'path' (files or directories to cache), 'key' (unique identifier for the created cache), and 'restore-keys' (fallback keys to match if an exact key is not found)."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Caches are immutable and scoped to a branch, the default branch, and pull requests."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementing Dependency Caching for Node.js"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Below is a complete workflow example demonstrating how to implement dependency caching for a Node.js application using package-lock.json for cache invalidation."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"name: Node.js CI with Caching
on: [push]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'
      - name: Cache dependencies
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.npm
          key: npm-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}
          restore-keys: |
            npm-
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci
      - name: Run build
        run: npm run build"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Optimization and Best Practices"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"To maximize the effectiveness of your caching strategy and avoid common pitfalls, follow these optimization guidelines:"},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use precise hashing: Base your cache keys on lockfiles like package-lock.json, yarn.lock, or requirements.txt rather than general directories."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Keep cache sizes reasonable: GitHub enforces a strict 10GB limit per repository for caches. Older caches are evicted automatically using a Least Recently Used (LRU) algorithm."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Leverage built-in setup actions: Many official setup actions (like setup-node, setup-python, setup-java) include built-in caching mechanisms that simplify configuration without manually calling actions/cache."}]
